sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of bards and minstrels. The name comes from the Welsh verb eistedd, to sit, and means a sitting together, a session of poets showing their skill before a noble patron. Koch 2006 records the first eisteddfod in Brut y Tywysogyon at the castle in Cardigan, also called Aberteifi, at Christmas 1176, when Lord Rhys ap Gruffudd of Deheubarth presided and bards competed for two Chair awards. It was proclaimed a year in advance throughout Wales, England, Scotland, and Ireland. The National Eisteddfod, held in the first full week of August, is the chief modern form, and the Welsh language is heard almost alone at it. In the nineteenth century it was rebuilt as a national event and tied to the Gorsedd of bards. The festival remains the major signifier of Welsh cultural distinctiveness.

okr.objective: Document the Eisteddfod as the Welsh festival of bards, from Koch 2006.
